analysis: The closest option combines organisational psychology and leadership, survey work and qualitative and statistical research, accounting and economics, strategy and AI-related workforce change. The workplace option provides sustained psychological health, development, assessment and evidence synthesis, with a bounded business setting. The institutional option connects political and legal structures, rights and policy analysis with labour-market microeconomics, organisational psychology, empirical research and negotiation. It does not train employment lawyers. Each directly responds to a target-supported direction rather than generic breadth.

Removed language-processing, molecular biology, general physiology, warfare and empire-history selections whose evidence did not sufficiently implement the intended workplace or institutional focus. Rebuilt their contributions through methods, organisations, finance and policy. Repaired the three original offering conflicts. Public law and constitutional law are no longer aligned to labour law; ethics is not philosophy of science, clinical assessment is not personnel selection, and evidence synthesis is not employee coaching. Retained eleven bounded positive alignments and meaningful blanks.

All pairwise curricula exceed thirty EC in each direction. The psychological-health option changes the academic priority and methods rather than merely changing its title. The institutional option has a sustained legal and political sequence. Three is the maximum, not a quota. Optional research remains outside the 180 EC.

BENECON311.name: Public Economics

BENENTR212.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation

BENENTR312.name: International Business & Governance

BENGATE101.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics

BENLEAD211.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure

BENLEAD311.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
BENLEAD311.contribution: examines behaviour, teams, culture and change and synthesises evidence about organisational practice

BENLEAD312.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking

GOSGATE102.name: Law, Society & Justice

GOSHIST111.name: Modern History
GOSHIST111.contribution: uses historical sources to study modern political, economic and cultural transformations

GOSLAWJ111.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
GOSLAWJ111.contribution: studies human rights through legal instruments, protection systems and philosophical argument

GOSLAWJ212.name: Introduction to Public International Law
GOSLAWJ212.contribution: Examines public international law, institutions and relationships with national legal systems.

GOSLAWJ312.name: Foundations of European Union Law
GOSLAWJ312.contribution: examines EU law, institutions, citizenship and the relationship between EU and domestic law

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.contribution: develops ethical reasoning about responsibilities and competing values relevant to decisions affecting employees

GOSPOLI112.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
GOSPOLI112.contribution: compares political institutions, democracy and political behaviour using empirical methods

GOSPOLI212.name: Theory of International Relations
GOSPOLI212.contribution: uses international relations theory and country research to analyse diplomacy, conflicts and institutions

GOSPOLI311.name: European Union Politics
GOSPOLI311.contribution: studies EU institutions and policymaking through empirical work on parliamentary amendments

GOSPOLI312.name: Public Policy Analysis
GOSPOLI312.contribution: Uses a case study to examine agenda-setting, policy choices and implementation in a global context.

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: uses sociological theories to investigate institutions, social boundaries and inequality

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: develops qualitative research through interviews, observation, coding and ethical reflection

GOSSOCI215.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
GOSSOCI215.contribution: studies social movements and environmental justice through cases and perspectives on gender, colonialism and political change

GOSSOCI311.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
GOSSOCI311.contribution: uses social theory and independent research to investigate civil-society organisations and movements

HCBCOGN112.name: Neurobiology
HCBCOGN112.contribution: examines neural regulation, sleep, mood and behaviour as biological foundations for psychological health; it is not occupational psychology

HCBGATE102.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
HCBGATE102.contribution: introduces psychological and neural explanations of behaviour, learning, personality and mental health

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.contribution: examines social influence, group behaviour and interpersonal processes using psychological research

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
HCBPSYC211.contribution: uses research design and statistical models to analyse and report behavioural findings

HCBPSYC212.name: Psychopathology
HCBPSYC212.contribution: examines biopsychosocial explanations of mental disorders and develops evidence appraisal relevant to understanding psychological health

HCBPSYC311.name: Medical & Health Psychology
HCBPSYC311.contribution: examines stress, health behaviour, health inequalities and interventions as foundations for understanding well-being

HCBPSYC312.name: Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies
HCBPSYC312.contribution: develops introductory knowledge of psychological tests, diagnostic interviews and treatments; this is clinical assessment rather than employee selection

HCBPSYC313.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
HCBPSYC313.contribution: develops systematic review and meta-analysis for evidence synthesis in behavioural and health research

HCBPSYC314.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
HCBPSYC314.contribution: examines development, relationships and change across adulthood and later life, providing foundations for thinking about employee development

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: uses persuasion theory and community projects to study and evaluate communication strategies

alignment.rationale: Both address survey design, psychological measurement and analysis; UCR uses leadership and social-experience applications.
Both examine motivation, teams, leadership and organisational culture.
Both introduce sociological theories and apply them to social life.
Both develop qualitative design, data collection and interpretation.
Both examine social influence, group behaviour and social psychological research.
Both develop statistical analysis for social and behavioural data.
Both study stress, health behaviour and well-being; UCR focuses on health and illness more broadly than the workplace.
Both address financial and management-accounting decisions; UCR does not specialise in personnel costs.
Both teach empirical design, operationalisation, measurement and introductory analysis.
Both introduce economic reasoning about markets and economic decisions.
Both address organisational strategy; UCR emphasises digital transformation.
